document.title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP on H100: --max-num-batched-tokens >= 24576 crashes EngineCore in fused qnorm/rope/kv-insert op; allocation invisible to memory profiler
document.body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM 0.23.0 (as packaged in `nvcr.io/nvidia/ai-dynamo/vllm-runtime:1.3.0`), torch 2.11.0+cu130
- 4x H100-80GB (HBM3), single node, `--tensor-parallel-size 4`
- Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` (revision `60d8d707`), `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--block-size 256`, MTP-1 speculative decoding, `max_model_len` 1048576, `cudagraph_mode FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`

### Description

Setting `--max-num-batched-tokens` to 24576 or 32768 causes a fatal EngineCore crash a few minutes into sustained load. The dangerous part: **the engine initializes cleanly, passes readiness, and answers single requests correctly** — it only dies once real traffic assembles a large batch, which makes this likely to reach production unnoticed.

Stack (identical across three crashes, on two different physical nodes):

```
vllm/models/deepseek_v4/attention.py:501  attention_impl
  -> :548 _fused_qnorm_rope_kv_insert
  -> torch.ops._C.fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_rope_quant_insert(...)
RuntimeError: torch_call_dispatcher( "aten::new_empty", "", stack.data(), TORCH_ABI_VERSION)
  API call failed at torch/csrc/stable/ops.h, line 933
-> EngineCore encountered a fatal error
-> vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError
```

Reproduction matrix (each row = one run of ~400 long-context requests at concurrency 16, agentic trace, ~64k ISL):

| `--max-num-batched-tokens` | Outcome |
|---|---|
| unset (default 8192) | stable, two independent full runs |
| 16384 | stable |
| 24576 | crash 9s into load (5/400 completed) |
| 32768 | crash (4/400 completed), reproduced on a second node |

Observed while serving through NVIDIA Dynamo's packaged runtime; the serving layer is not in the stack, and an equivalent `vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash -tp 4 --max-num-batched-tokens 24576` under sustained long-context load is expected to reproduce.

### Root-cause analysis (from reading v0.23.0 source)

In `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/attention.py`, `_fused_qnorm_rope_kv_insert` (~L508):

1. **The memory profiler never exercises this kernel.** During the profile run `attn_metadata` is not a dict, so the method early-returns a padded tensor and the fused op never fires ("Profile run: kernel doesn't fire"). Any allocation internal to `fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_rope_quant_insert` that scales with the number of batched tokens is invisible to memory accounting — matching the observed behavior exactly (init/readiness pass; death only when a large batch first assembles).
2. **The stable-ABI wrapper masks the real error.** `new_empty ... API call failed at torch/csrc/stable/ops.h:933` is consistent with an allocation failure inside the op being swallowed by the stable-ABI layer instead of surfacing as an actionable CUDA OOM.
3. **Corroboration:** on the same model with a non-fused path (DP4), raising `--max-num-batched-tokens` produced a clean CUDA OOM, with vLLM's profiler having under-estimated peak activation by ~2.8x — same root (profile-run blind spot to batched-token-scaled allocations), different error surface.

Suggested fixes, in increasing depth: (a) make the profile path account for the fused op's allocations (allocate what the kernel would); (b) surface the underlying CUDA error through the stable-ABI wrapper; (c) validate `max_num_batched_tokens` against the kernel's allocation model at init and fail fast with a clear message.

First reported with full artifacts at ai-dynamo/dynamo#12972. Disclosure: the crash was found by an AI agent running automated optimization testing; the source analysis and this report were prepared with AI assistance and human review.
